entries.text: To address the human factors angle of the Alaska door plug incident, senior leadership called me up to see if I could come up with a human factors or AI solution to prevent recurrences.
entries.intent: Establish responsibility for a consequential safety problem

entries.text: The immediate investigation highlighted failures in documentation protocols, but a deeper analysis revealed a more insidious systemic issue: compounding rework cycles.
entries.intent: Distinguish documentation symptoms from rework-system causes

entries.text: When errors occurred, the process for rectifying them induced new opportunities for error, creating a negative feedback loop that accelerated organizational friction and obscured baseline safety metrics.
entries.intent: Explain how correction can create further error

entries.text: To address the issue, we implemented two parallel solutions.
entries.intent: Organize the response into two parallel interventions

entries.text: First, by addressing the immediate need for rigorous, accessible documentation and targeted training.
entries.intent: Meet the immediate documentation and training need

entries.text: Second, and more critically, we fundamentally redesigned the workflow using specialized software tools designed to "short-circuit" rework cycles.
entries.intent: Address the deeper workflow loop

entries.text: By introducing digital guardrails and forcing function protocols, we ensured that necessary rework did not compound into further errors, stabilizing the production pipeline.
entries.intent: Explain how guardrails stabilize the process

entries.text: I want to note that while Senior Leadership came to me for a specific AI solution, we managed to successfully de-risk a GraphRAG solution implementation before it resulted in any cost to Boeing.
entries.intent: Show willingness to reject an unsuitable AI solution early

entries.text: I'm a big fan of fail-fast testing in the early stages of solution workshopping, and AI solutions shouldn't be applied in situations that are inappropriate to their strengths.
entries.intent: State a preference for testing fit before investing

entries.intent: Explain why project details cannot be pictured

entries.text: Industry Experimental Design: While at InfoSytex working on military contracts using a secret clearance, I applied experimental design principles to real-world testing environments.
entries.intent: Ground research methods in demanding field work

entries.text: This required rigorous structuring of tests for novel systems to extract usable data in chaotic, high-stakes operational contexts.
entries.intent: Explain the challenge of extracting usable experimental evidence

entries.text: Biometric Data Wrangling: A core component of my research involved creating pipelines to translate raw physiological signals into actionable system intelligence.
entries.intent: Describe translating physiology into operational information

entries.text: We took noisy streams of eye-tracking and raw biometric data and filtered them into discrete markers indicative of pilot cognitive state.
entries.intent: Specify the transformation from noisy signals to cognitive markers

entries.text: This data became a real-time input for adaptive systems to recognize when an operator was becoming taxed.
entries.intent: Connect the markers to real-time adaptation

entries.text: Dissertation: "Capturing Intentional Testing of an Automated System" My dissertation revolved around the idea that we aren't passive observers of systems we interact with.
entries.intent: Reject the picture of users as passive observers

entries.text: Rather, I made the case that we actively seek out information through a testing process that I defined, captured, and analyzed.
entries.intent: Describe defining and studying intentional system testing

entries.text: The Broader Scope: I have served on three distinct AI Governance Councils at Boeing, acting as the primary conduit for the human side of the technical problem statement.
entries.intent: Establish experience representing human concerns in AI governance

entries.text: My current role on the Human Engineering through AI-Teaming (HEAT) subcouncil is the latest iteration of this ongoing work.
entries.intent: Locate the current council role within continued work

entries.text: Specific Achievements: My governance work involves designing intake processes that force development teams to confront human-system integration challenges early.
entries.intent: Describe governance that surfaces integration problems early

entries.text: Prior to Boeing's most recent AI restructuring, we built the foundation in governance structures that allowed the current administration to take off so quickly.
entries.intent: Credit earlier foundations for later progress

entries.text: Most recently, however, I am leading the charge in Human Factors at Boeing in making the tools that help make governance automatic.
entries.intent: Return to tools that make good practice automatic

entries.text: Cross-Domain Leadership: I led efforts to bridge the gap between Boeing's commercial safety culture and the unique demands of the BDS military side regarding AI integration.
entries.intent: Describe bridging distinct safety cultures

entries.text: This included establishing frameworks for determining equivalent levels of safety for AI-enabled systems and engagement with the FAA representatives on aligning emerging safety regulations with technical reality.
entries.intent: Make the bridge concrete through assurance and regulatory work

entries.text: UAV Swarms: Fresh out of my PhD program, I stepped into a lead design role for a military-industrial development team creating control systems for UAV swarms.
entries.intent: Establish responsibility for an early demanding design role

entries.text: The target user was not the pilot, but the second-seater operating in a high-intensity battlespace.
entries.intent: Identify the actual operator rather than assuming the pilot

entries.text: The core innovation was a context-aware UI paradigm—dynamically modulating information density based on real-time operator workload assessment.
entries.intent: State adaptation to workload as the core innovation

entries.text: The UI was designed to constrict or expand information availability—taking over lower-level tasks autonomously when the battle space became chaotic, and returning control when cognitive bandwidth became available.
entries.intent: Describe sharing task responsibility as workload changes

entries.text: Testing & Validation: These designs weren't theoretical.
entries.intent: Emphasize that the design was implemented

entries.text: They were fully built and then we validated them in full-scale mock-up piloting environments, demoing the adaptive capabilities with ex-pilot SMEs to ensure the system reduced, rather than exacerbated, cognitive burden.
entries.intent: Describe realistic validation with experienced users

entries.text: While we did do live flight-testing, the meatiest experimental design was done for and with a nearby lab.
